hypotheses.justification: The statement still holds when x = 0. `0 ∈ w.toValuationSubring` is true (`zero_mem`). `Place.ord` is defined in Def_AlgebraicCurve_DivisorClassGroup.lean:122 as `-(WithZero.log (v.adicValuation f))`, and `Place.ord_zero : v.ord 0 = 0` (line 125) gives `0 ≤ w.ord 0`. So both sides are true. New proof: `by_cases hx : x = 0`. If `x = 0`, substitute and close with `simp [Place.ord_zero, zero_mem]`. Otherwise run the existing `rw` chain, which needs `x ≠ 0` only for `w.adicValuation_ne_zero hx`.

It is included only because it is an instance on the included variable `N`. The statement does not need it to elaborate. `modularFunctionFieldBar` (Def_ModularCurve_ArithmeticGalois.lean:109-113) is declared in a section with only `variable (N : ℕ)` and no `NeZero`. It is `laurentBaseChange (AlgebraicClosure ℚ) (modularFunctionFieldFull N)`, so it elaborates without `NeZero N`. `Place K F` (DivisorClassGroup.lean:20-22) only needs `[Field K] [Field F] [Algebra K F]`. The proof uses only generic lemmas about `Place` (`mem_iff_adicValuation_le_one`, `ord`, `adicValuation_ne_zero`) and `WithZero` lemmas, none of which involve N. So `omit [NeZero N] in` leaves the statement and proof unchanged. This hypothesis and `hx` are independent: either can be removed, and so can both together.
